> I have run simulations for each model and fit these data to each other model. I have done this 100 times, each time tallying which model won (fits are compared by Bayes factors using the `bridgesampling` package). This results in a confusion matrix at the end.

```{r rmd-setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::knit_hooks$set(purl = knitr::hook_purl) # creates an R file upon knitting the Rmd
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8)
```

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
rm(list = ls())
library(tidyverse)
library(bridgesampling)
main_dir <- "~/research/climate-RL-mod/"
recov_dir <- paste0(main_dir, "4_model_recovery/")
util_dir <- paste0(main_dir, "9_utilities/")
plot <- new.env()
source(paste0(util_dir, "plot_utils.R"), local = plot)
```

Model comparison is done using Bayes factors, as calculated by the `bridgesampling` package. I first compare fits for models `0_nolearning` and `1_std`. If BF~10~ > 3 (moderate evidence), model 1 is the winner. If BF~10~ < 3, model 0 is the winner, because in this situation either there is insufficient evidence for model 1 (in which case the simpler model wins), or there is evidence for model 0. We then compare fits for models `1_std` and `2_LRN_gauss`, and again, if BF~21~ > 3, model 2 wins, and model 1 wins otherwise. I then compare the two winning models using the same criteria to find the final winner.

```{r create-dat}
n_runs <- 1

confusion <- data.frame(
  sim_mod = (rep(0:2, each = 3)),
  fit_mod = (rep(0:2, 3)),
  p = 0
)

for (sim_model in as.character(0:2)) {
  winning_models <- readRDS(sprintf("%ssim%s/winning_models.rds", recov_dir, sim_model))
  for (run in 1:n_runs) {
    confusion <- confusion %>%
      mutate(p = if_else(sim_mod == sim_model & fit_mod == winning_models$winner[run],
                         p + 1/n_runs,
                         p))
  }
}
```

# Confusion matrix
```{r make-confusion-matrix}
ggplot(confusion, aes(x = sim_mod, y = fit_mod, fill = p)) +
  geom_tile(color = "black") +
  geom_text(aes(label = p), size = 18, size.unit = "pt") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = plot$my_teal, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Simulated model", y = "Fitted model") +
  plot$my_theme
```
